answer: Registration binds an identity to one attested chip, $60, with a non-exportable maker-certified key, held 180 days. The chip sits behind a prism window in a juniper frame, whose refraction pattern and grain are hashed as a fingerprint. Each epoch a beacon sends a nonce and light pulse; the chip signs only after sensing it through the prism, in 2 seconds. A fingerprint mismatch or a twice-registered serial zeroes both. One identity pays $60 once; 1,000 fakes pay $60,000 for 1,000 units, since a shared unit leaves the second registration fingerprintless, its replies failing the registry check.
